title: Provider, process-lock and workspace inventory adapters
description:
Objective: land the production enumerators for the provider/process/launch-lock class and the workspace class, registered into the recovery-inventory port registry. Slice 2 of 3 from task-0325dcf7ee744123b40cf583230c7b6a, split by architect-d46fcb95 on human direction 2026-08-09.

Hard dependency: task-00956ac383784e81b0345bbf09256323 (Recovery-inventory contract and coverage protocol) must land first - it owns the class set, the item shape, the coverage proof, the INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer and the port registry this slice plugs into. Do not restate or re-derive any of them here.

MEASURED PRESENT at 2026-08-09 by architect-d46fcb95 - every primitive this slice calls already exists, so nothing here needs a prerequisite:
- provider capability probes: packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-probe.ts (probeClaudeRuntime, capabilityStatus) and providers/codex/codex-probe.ts (probeCodexRuntime, capabilityStatus).
- launch-lock records: packages/runner/src/supervisor/launch-lock.ts (LaunchLockRegistration, parseLaunchLockRegistration, registerLaunchLock, bindsClaim). NOTE: this module is deliberately NOT root-exported; import it relatively from inside the package, do not publish it.
- process observation: packages/runner/src/supervisor/process-observation.ts (BoundProcessObservation, intakeProcessObservation). Its own comment is the rule this slice must honour - "UNOBSERVED is not death. Only an observed exit or signal proves an end."
- workspace manifests: packages/runner/src/workspace/workspace-manifest.ts (buildInputManifest, buildResultManifest) and workspace-contract.ts (WorkspaceInputManifest, WorkspaceInputEntry, WorkspaceTreeEntry).

Deliverable: packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory/provider-lock-inventory.ts (+ .js bridge) and workspace-inventory.ts (+ .js bridge) plus focused tests, each registering itself as a class enumerator through the contract slice's port registry.

NOT in scope: the contract, coverage protocol or aggregate (slice 1); Git refs, integration targets or artifact objects (slice 3); scheduler resource rows; adopt/quarantine decisions; project embargo; tests/fault.

Owned paths: packages/runner/src/recovery-inventory/provider-lock-inventory.{ts,js}, workspace-inventory.{ts,js}, their focused tests, and the two-line registration edit in the slice-1 aggregate. This slice does NOT edit index.ts or index-surface.test.ts - slice 1 owns the root seam.

Consumer (global rail Clause 1): daemon coordinator task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test
definitionOfDone: The provider/process/launch-lock enumerator calls the shipped probeClaudeRuntime/probeCodexRuntime capability surfaces and the launch-lock and process-observation records, binding every item to its class, stable external identity, observed disposition facts and source proof digest; it never treats a quiet process or an empty probe result as absence.

The workspace enumerator reads real workspace input/result manifests through the shipped workspace-manifest surface and binds each workspace item the same way, refusing rather than merging when two entries claim one external identity.

An unavailable enumerator, an unsupported or absent provider capability, a truncated or over-limit result, and a missing negative proof each return RECOVERY_INVENTORY_COVERAGE_UNKNOWN at layer INVENTORY_ADAPTER with truth UNKNOWN; partial items never upgrade the class to COMPLETE.

Both enumerators are registered with the slice-1 port registry and a test proves the aggregate reports COMPLETE for these two classes only when the enumerator actually proved completeness, and UNKNOWN in every other case including the absent-registration case.

Focused tests exercise real temporary filesystem bytes and the shipped provider-probe surfaces rather than a reimplemented fixture authority, assert each covered class generated at least one coverage case with a non-zero asserted count, pin the exact code and INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer on every refusal, and mutation-check that the coverage handling is reddenable.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test exits 0, with any residual red attributed to foreign paths against a recorded merge-base baseline.
taskRails: A configured class requires complete enumeration or a verifiable negative proof; an empty list, a quiet process, an absent optional probe, or a mock response is never COMPLETE by itself.

Reuse the shipped probes, launch-lock records, process observation and workspace manifests. Do not reimplement any of their authority inside this module or inside a test helper; a property must be asserted against the production surface.
supervisor/launch-lock.ts is intentionally unpublished. Import it relatively within the package and do not add it to the @moe/runner root seam.
Tests assert the exact stable reason code and the INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer, and assert non-zero generated class coverage.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; this cap is per file, not per task.

implementationPlan.description:
RE-MEASURE (read-only; this step writes nothing), then read the ruling that changes the shape of this task.

I verified every primitive the description names. All are PRESENT and, unusually for this board, the description is ACCURATE on them — confirm anyway, the staleness rail binds in both directions:
  packages/runner/src/supervisor/launch-lock.ts:29 LaunchLockRegistration, :64 parseLaunchLockRegistration, :76 bindsClaim, :90 registerLaunchLock
  packages/runner/src/supervisor/process-observation.ts:21 BoundProcessObservation, :60 intakeProcessObservation
  packages/runner/src/workspace/workspace-manifest.ts:62 buildInputManifest, :189 buildResultManifest
  packages/runner/src/workspace/workspace-contract.ts:59 WorkspaceInputEntry, :66 WorkspaceInputManifest, :91 WorkspaceTreeEntry
  packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-probe.ts:56 probeClaudeRuntime, :89 capabilityStatus
  packages/runner/src/providers/codex/codex-probe.ts:93 probeCodexRuntime, :102 capabilityStatus
Slice 1 is landed AND tracked at HEAD (git ls-tree confirms 7 files): recovery-inventory-contract.ts 207 lines, recovery-inventory-shape.ts 223, recovery-inventory.ts 378, recovery-inventory.test.ts 615, plus .js bridges.

*** THE RULING — DO NOT EDIT THE SLICE-1 AGGREGATE. *** The description lists "the two-line registration edit in the slice-1 aggregate" as an owned path. Do NOT make that edit; there is nothing there to edit. recovery-inventory.ts:53 createRecoveryInventoryRegistry(registrations) takes an IMMUTABLE CALLER-SUPPLIED TUPLE, and its doc comment rejects the alternative in terms naming this exact hazard: "Registration is an immutable caller-supplied tuple rather than a module-global registry: a global would be order-dependent, race-prone across concurrent collections, and would let a sibling adapter slice change this aggregate's behaviour by importing it." Slice 2 IS that sibling adapter slice. Instead each new module EXPORTS a RecoveryInventoryRegistration constant; tests compose their own registry and the daemon coordinator composes the real one. Your final diff must show ZERO changes to recovery-inventory.ts, index.ts and index-surface.test.ts.

NAME COLLISION: capabilityStatus is exported by BOTH probe modules over different profile/capability types. Importing both unaliased will not compile — alias them (claudeCapabilityStatus / codexCapabilityStatus).

TDD RED — write provider-lock-inventory.test.ts before any implementation. Drive every case through the real collectRecoveryInventory with a registry composed from the exported registration, so assertions land on the production surface.

Cover, pinning the EXACT reason code AND the INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer on each refusal (never merely "it failed"):
  - Happy path: real launch-lock registrations and process observations enumerate to items bound to PROVIDER_PROCESS_LAUNCH_LOCK with stable external identity, observed disposition facts and a sourceProofDigest. COMPLETE only when completeness was actually proven.
  - A QUIET PROCESS IS NOT ABSENCE — the most important case here. process-observation.ts states the rule: "UNOBSERVED is not death. Only an observed exit or signal proves an end." An unobserved process must NOT be omitted and must NOT be reported as terminated; it either appears as an item carrying its unobserved disposition or drives UNKNOWN. Assert this explicitly.
  - Empty probe result with no negative proof -> code RECOVERY_INVENTORY_COVERAGE_UNKNOWN, layer INVENTORY_ADAPTER, reason NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING. An empty list is never COMPLETE by itself.
  - Absent/unsupported provider capability, driven through the real capabilityStatus returning "UNSUPPORTED" -> reason CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED.
  - Port throws or unavailable -> ENUMERATOR_UNAVAILABLE. Over-ceiling -> RESULT_OVER_LIMIT. complete:false -> RESULT_TRUNCATED.
  - Two entries claiming one external identity REFUSE rather than merge.

Put test doubles at the port boundary the probes already define (input.port.report()), so the real probe and real capabilityStatus stay in the path under test. Do NOT reimplement probe authority in a fixture — taskRail 2 and epic rail 6 both forbid it. Assert a non-zero generated case count for the class so a sweep producing nothing cannot pass.

GREEN — implement provider-lock-inventory.ts plus its one-line sibling .js bridge.

Export an enumerator and a `RecoveryInventoryRegistration` constant for class PROVIDER_PROCESS_LAUNCH_LOCK. Compose the three shipped authorities and add none of your own: probeClaudeRuntime / probeCodexRuntime with the aliased capabilityStatus for provider capability; parseLaunchLockRegistration and bindsClaim for launch-lock records; intakeProcessObservation for process disposition.

IMPORT launch-lock.ts RELATIVELY from inside the package. It is deliberately unpublished — do NOT add it to the @moe/runner root seam, and do not edit index.ts or index-surface.test.ts at all; slice 1 owns that seam.

Fail closed on every uncertain branch: return UNAVAILABLE or UNSUPPORTED rather than an empty ENUMERATED, and set complete:false with a null negativeProofDigest when you cannot prove you saw everything. Never let a quiet process read as an ended one.

THE .js BRIDGE IS NOT OPTIONAL AND ITS ABSENCE IS INVISIBLE — omitting it fails neither tsc nor vitest and breaks only the plain-Node entrypoint. Match the existing sibling bridges exactly including the trailing LF; verify with `od -c`.

Target <=250 physical lines, split before 400, measured with `grep -c ''` (PowerShell Measure-Object -Line undercounts by skipping blank lines).

TDD RED then GREEN for the WORKSPACE class — workspace-inventory.test.ts, then workspace-inventory.ts plus its .js bridge.

DoD 5 requires REAL TEMPORARY FILESYSTEM BYTES here, not an in-memory double: build actual manifests through the shipped buildInputManifest (workspace-manifest.ts:62) and buildResultManifest (:189) over a real temp directory, and bind each workspace item with the same class/identity/facts/sourceProofDigest discipline as the provider enumerator.

Create the temp directory with mkdtemp under the OS temp root, NEVER inside the repo — a stray fixture directory in a commit breaks epic rail 5's no-scratch-files clause. Remove it in an afterEach that runs even when the test fails, recursive and forced, since this host is win32.

Mandatory cases, each pinning the exact code and INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer:
  - Two entries claiming one external identity REFUSE rather than merge — DoD 2 names this explicitly. Compare with identityKey (shape:121) and expect RECOVERY_INVENTORY_EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE, not silent last-writer-wins.
  - Truncated or over-limit manifest results -> RESULT_TRUNCATED / RESULT_OVER_LIMIT.
  - Missing negative proof on an empty workspace -> NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING, never COMPLETE.
Assert a non-zero generated case count for the WORKSPACE class.

Same rules as the provider module: relative imports, no root-seam edit, .js bridge with od -c verified trailing LF, <=250 lines target.

DoD 4 — prove the registration seam end to end, WITHOUT editing the aggregate (step 1 ruling).

In one of the two test files, compose a registry with createRecoveryInventoryRegistry([providerLockRegistration, workspaceRegistration]) and drive collectRecoveryInventory. Assert:
  - Both classes report COMPLETE only when the enumerator actually proved completeness: items enumerated AND complete:true AND, for an empty result, a non-null negativeProofDigest.
  - Every other case reports UNKNOWN with code RECOVERY_INVENTORY_COVERAGE_UNKNOWN at layer INVENTORY_ADAPTER and its specific reason.
  - THE ABSENT-REGISTRATION CASE, which DoD 4 names explicitly: compose a registry OMITTING one of the two classes while it REMAINS in configuredClasses, and assert that class answers UNKNOWN with reason ENUMERATOR_UNREGISTERED. This is slice 1's "we never looked" invariant — the class must not vanish from the report.
  - Partial items never upgrade a class to COMPLETE, and a later success never launders an earlier UNKNOWN.

Assert coverage proofs by whole-object equality on class, truth, code, reason and layer — not by a .length or truthiness check, so an extra or swapped proof fails.

DoD 5 mutation drills — coverage handling that cannot go red proves nothing. Run each drill, confirm the NAMED case kills it, revert, and confirm green before the next. Record the exact failing assertion for each.

  1. Make the provider enumerator return { status: "ENUMERATED", items: [], complete: true, negativeProofDigest: null } for an empty probe. The NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING case must go RED — this is the "an empty list is not COMPLETE" invariant.
  2. Make a quiet/unobserved process read as terminated. The unobserved-is-not-death case must go RED.
  3. Make the workspace enumerator merge two entries sharing one external identity instead of refusing. The duplicate case must go RED naming RECOVERY_INVENTORY_EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE.
  4. Drop one registration from the composed registry. The ENUMERATOR_UNREGISTERED case must go RED rather than the class silently disappearing from the report.

Back up mutated bytes OUTSIDE the repo and restore with verified sha256 equality.

SHARED-WORKTREE HAZARD: a foreign completion hook can whole-tree commit your mutation while it sits on disk — three such commits landed today (71af97c, a646660, 1e3057a). After each revert check BOTH `git diff -- <file>` AND `git status --porcelain <file>`; a clean diff alone is not proof. Leave no drill residue.

DoD 6 — verification and adversarial review. Run the exact gate LAST, fresh and foreground:

  pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test

Both legs must exit 0 with nonzero discovery. Recorded baseline on this package from the sibling task: 43 files / 1366 tests. Your run must show MORE files — two new test files. A flat file count means your tests never ran.

Path-attributed baseline per project rail: record repo-wide failures at merge-base and at HEAD, require the (HEAD minus merge-base) failing set intersected with owned paths to be EMPTY, and disclose foreign red verbatim with exact lines and paths. Foreign red INSIDE @moe/runner is a BLOCK, not a disclosure — the baseline never excuses package-local red.

Adversarial review before complete_task:
- Did I edit recovery-inventory.ts, index.ts or index-surface.test.ts? I must NOT have. Confirm with `git diff --stat`.
- Is launch-lock.ts still unpublished — absent from the root seam?
- Does any test assert against a helper that reimplements probe, manifest or observation authority? That is the epic rail 6 defect; properties must go through collectRecoveryInventory or the shipped surface.
- Does every refusal test pin the exact reason code AND the INVENTORY_ADAPTER layer, not merely that it refused?
- Did each of the two classes generate at least one coverage case with a non-zero asserted count?
- Both .js bridges present with trailing LF, od -c verified?
- No temp fixture directory left inside the repo; no scratch or generated-evidence files in the diff.
- Per-file line counts under 400, target 250, measured with `grep -c ''`.
- GLOBAL RAIL CLAUSE 1: name daemon coordinator task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa as the production consumer in your completion evidence. Do NOT land the consumer edge here.
- Stage and commit by EXPLICIT pathspec over the six owned files only. Never git add -A.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
EDIT THE SLICE-1 AGGREGATE TO REGISTER THE TWO ENUMERATORS — REJECTED, and this is the plan's most important decision. The task description lists "the two-line registration edit in the slice-1 aggregate" among the owned paths, so a worker following it literally would edit recovery-inventory.ts. There is nothing there to edit: createRecoveryInventoryRegistry (recovery-inventory.ts:53) takes an immutable caller-supplied tuple, and the function's own doc comment rejects the alternative in terms that name this exact hazard — "a global would be order-dependent, race-prone across concurrent collections, and would let a sibling adapter slice change this aggregate's behaviour by importing it." Slice 2 is precisely that sibling adapter slice. So each module exports a RecoveryInventoryRegistration constant, tests compose their own registry, and the daemon coordinator composes the real one. Zero aggregate edits, and slice 3 can land the same way without colliding.

UNIT-TESTING A PRIVATE MAPPING HELPER FOR THE DoD 3 REFUSALS — REJECTED. Enumerators return a RecoveryInventoryPortReading; the aggregate mints the coverage proof, code and reason. Asserting refusals against a helper inside the new module would test a reimplementation of the aggregate's authority, which epic rail 6 and taskRail 2 both forbid. Every DoD 3 case is therefore driven end to end through collectRecoveryInventory.

IN-MEMORY WORKSPACE DOUBLES — REJECTED. DoD 5 requires real temporary filesystem bytes for the workspace class, so manifests are built through the shipped buildInputManifest/buildResultManifest over a real mkdtemp directory outside the repo.

REIMPLEMENTING PROBE AUTHORITY IN A FIXTURE — REJECTED. The probes already define their own port boundary (input.port.report()); doubles belong there, keeping the real probe and the real capabilityStatus inside the path under test.

NOTE ON PLAN SIZE: an earlier submission was rejected at 11 distinct affectedFiles because I had declared read-only reference modules (the contract, shape, aggregate, probes, launch-lock, workspace manifest) as affected. They are READ, not written. affectedFiles now lists only the six files this task creates; the reference paths and their line numbers live in the step text. The deliverable is unchanged and matches the description exactly: two enumerator modules, two .js bridges, two focused tests. No SPIDR split is warranted — the task is correctly sized.

planningNotes.risks:
1. EDITING THE SLICE-1 AGGREGATE. The description invites it; the design forbids it. A registration edit inside recovery-inventory.ts recreates the module-global coupling slice 1 explicitly refused, and it would collide with slice 3 doing the same. The final diff must show zero changes to that file.

2. TREATING SILENCE AS ABSENCE — the failure this entire class exists to prevent. A quiet process, an empty probe result, or an empty manifest must never read as COMPLETE. Any empty result needs a non-null negativeProofDigest or it is UNKNOWN with NEGATIVE_PROOF_MISSING.

3. ASSERTING REFUSALS AGAINST A LOCAL HELPER instead of collectRecoveryInventory. The code and layer are minted by the aggregate; a test that checks a private mapping function proves only that the module agrees with itself.

4. capabilityStatus COLLIDES between the two probe modules — alias both imports.

5. THE .js BRIDGE IS INVISIBLE WHEN MISSING — it fails neither tsc nor vitest and breaks only the plain-Node entrypoint. Two are required; verify the trailing LF with od -c.

6. TEMP DIRECTORIES ON WINDOWS. Use mkdtemp under the OS temp root, never inside the repo, and remove recursively and forcefully in an afterEach that runs on failure. A leftover fixture directory in a commit breaks epic rail 5.

7. SHARED WORKTREE. Foreign whole-tree commits landed three times today (71af97c, a646660, 1e3057a). An empty `git status` over owned paths is AMBIGUOUS — swept into a foreign commit, or never committed. Resolve per file with `git rev-parse --verify HEAD:<path>`, and never amend, reset or stash a foreign commit.

8. PUBLISHING launch-lock.ts. It is deliberately unpublished — import it relatively and keep it out of the root seam. This slice must not touch index.ts or index-surface.test.ts at all; slice 1 owns that seam and slice 3 is queued behind it.
